claims.text: GitHub Actions runs the workflows a repository defines as YAML files in the .github/workflows directory; the on: key lists the events that trigger a workflow.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Workflow syntax for GitHub Actions (on); About workflows

claims.text: workflow_dispatch lets a workflow be started manually; the 'Run workflow' button appears in the repository's Actions tab when the workflow file is on the default branch.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Events that trigger workflows > workflow_dispatch; Manually running a workflow

claims.text: A workflow run is made of one or more jobs; each job runs on a runner chosen by runs-on; ci.yml@stage-1 has one job, lab, with runs-on: ubuntu-24.04.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Workflow syntax (jobs.<job_id>.runs-on); examples/don-hang @ stage-1 .github/workflows/ci.yml:8-11

claims.text: Each GitHub-hosted runner is a new VM for the job (runs-on: ubuntu-24.04 = Ubuntu 24.04 Linux), with the runner application and other tools preinstalled, but without the repository's files until actions/checkout checks the commit out.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: About GitHub-hosted runners; actions/checkout README

claims.text: A job's steps run in order on the same runner, so a later step sees files an earlier step left on the machine, including tools an action such as setup-dotnet installed (environment variable changes are not kept between steps).
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Workflow syntax (jobs.<job_id>.steps: each step runs in the runner environment, in order); Understanding GitHub Actions

claims.text: A uses: step runs an action referenced as owner/repo@ref (e.g. actions/setup-dotnet@v4); with: passes the action's inputs; a run: step runs command-line programs in the runner's shell.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Workflow syntax (steps[*].uses, steps[*].with, steps[*].run)

claims.text: A run: step fails when its command exits with a non-zero code; steps without if: use the default success() check and are skipped once a previous step failed.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Workflow syntax (exit codes and error action preference; steps[*].if: default status check success())

claims.text: if: failure() runs a step when any previous step of the job failed; if: always() runs it whatever happened; such steps running does not change the job's failed result.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Expressions > Status check functions (failure, always)

claims.text: Without actions/checkout the workspace holds none of the repository's files: neither global.json, which setup-dotnet is told to read via global-json-file, nor DonHang.slnx for dotnet build.
claims.source_hint: actions/checkout README; GitHub Docs: About GitHub-hosted runners

claims.text: git diff --exit-code exits with 1 when there are differences and 0 when there are none.
shell: bash on Linux runs the commands with bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0} (stop at first failing command, fail a pipe if any part fails); without shell:, bash -e {0} is used.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Workflow syntax (defaults.run.shell / jobs.<job_id>.steps[*].shell); log of run 36301845534 shows both lines

claims.text: name: sets the label shown for the step in the run's list of steps; the 'Say what went wrong' step writes an ::error workflow command so the log tail appears on the run's page, then prints docker compose logs.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Workflow syntax (steps[*].name); Workflow commands (::error); ci.yml@stage-1:50-56

claims.text: ci.yml@stage-1 step order after 'Test the solution': Analyze and test DonHang.App, Start the lab, Run every lesson script and capture its output, Fail if any captured output changed, Say what went wrong (if: failure()), Stop the lab (if: always()).
Skipped steps appear in the run's step list as skipped (not failed).
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Using workflow run logs / Viewing workflow run history

claims.text: run: actions/checkout@v4 is passed to bash as a command; bash looks for a program at that path, finds none and the step fails (exit 127), the code is not fetched.
claims.source_hint: bash manual: Command Search and Execution (name containing slash is executed as path; 127 when not found)

claims.text: The push event runs a workflow when a commit or a tag is pushed; a tag is a fixed name for one commit.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Events that trigger workflows > push; git-tag docs
